answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity: every identity must lock a bond, like quartz formed under pressure. Rewards are split not by headcount but by verifiable useful work, so spinning up thousands of fake agents yields nothing — the nectar of profit flows only to identities with attested contribution history. Newcomers start under a willow of scrutiny: their early attestations carry little weight until diverse, established peers vouch for them, so faking a trusted network of identities costs far more than any reward the sybil cluster could extract.
